clue.text: Agree to redraft of letters

indicators.note: to redraft is to write out again in a new form, so the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone consents to a revised version of some correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redraft' looks like a noun naming a document, but it signals that the nine letters of OF LETTERS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to settle for something is to accept or agree to it, often as less than hoped.

clue.text: Rubbish loaded up into metal skip

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards
the answer is found within the run of letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Junk being piled into a metal skip, a builder's waste container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' hides ETALS in 'metal skip', and 'up' reverses it. 'Rubbish' is the verb: to criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate something is to criticise it severely, to rubbish it.

clue.text: Objects to a few kids at movie getting fidgety

indicators.note: restless fidgeting moves things about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Children who get restless at the cinema irritate other filmgoers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting fidgety' rearranges all fifteen letters of 'a few kids at movie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to take a dim view of something is to disapprove of it, to object.

clue.text: Pining character in new book, completely upset

indicators.note: everything is turned over, so the whole assembled string is read backwards
the character's letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: vol, volume, is a book
a role is a character in a play

explanation.surface: A yearning figure in a fresh novel, thoroughly distraught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'completely upset' reverses the whole string NROLEVOL, not just one piece; 'in' places the character between new and book.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovelorn means unhappy through unrequited love, pining for someone.

clue.text: Queue briefly for the solution

indicators.note: a brief version is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to queue is to form a line

explanation.surface: A brief reply to a puzzle: queue up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queue' is the phrase FORM A LINE; 'briefly' cuts its last letter. 'for the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Formalin is a solution of formaldehyde in water, used as a preservative.

clue.text: German version of Steptoe and Son

indicators.note: a version is a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A German adaptation of the British TV sitcom Steptoe and Son.
explanation.walkthrough: Steptoe and Son was a British sitcom about a father and son who were rag-and-bone men, collecting junk with a horse and cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the two Steptoes were rag dealers, collecting old clothes and scrap from the street.

clue.text: Note rolls filled with uncooked meat

indicators.note: the turned letters are packed around the next piece, as a filling sits inside
something that rolls over turns round, so the letters for note are read backwards

parts.note: NB, nota bene, is the abbreviation used to mark a note
uncooked means raw

explanation.surface: A recipe note: bread rolls stuffed with raw meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' looks like bread but signals a reversal, giving BN; 'filled with' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Brawn is a cold preparation of pressed meat from a pig's head set in jelly.

clue.text: Detailed forthright account describing unknown French author

indicators.note: to describe is also to draw round, so these letters encircle the next
de-tailed: the tail, the last letter, is removed

parts.note: bald means blunt or forthright, as in a bald statement
Z is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A frank, thorough report about a mysterious French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like thorough but means losing the tail. 'describing' means drawing round, so it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Honoré de Balzac was a nineteenth-century French novelist, author of La Comédie humaine.

clue.text: Cool customer from Brazil?

parts.note: a Brazil nut has a tough shell, and a cool, unflappable person is difficult to read or break

explanation.surface: A calm person who comes from Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brazil is a kind of nut with a very hard shell; the phrase also describes a person hard to influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a tough problem or person, punning on the literal nut from Brazil.

clue.text: Nation's leaders attending mass meeting of workers, as you'd expect

parts.note: the leading letters, the first two, of Nation
TU, trade union, is an organisation of workers
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: National leaders turn up at a union demonstration, unsurprisingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting of workers' looks like one phrase: 'mass meeting' gives RALLY and 'workers' TU; 'attending' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: naturally means of course, as might be expected.

clue.text: Invite round, say, to eat endless toast

indicators.note: one piece eating another takes it inside, so these letters go within the first

parts.note: to aver is to state or say

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the drinking toast is dropped

parts.note: skol is a Scandinavian drinking toast

explanation.surface: Suggesting you invite a guest over for something to eat on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toast' is the drink-raising kind, not bread; 'endless' trims it and 'to eat' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: asking someone over is inviting them round to your home.

clue.text: Female with inclination to ignore overture, from him?

definitions.text: Female with inclination to ignore overture, from him?

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl or woman

indicators.note: an overture is an opening, so ignoring it drops the first letter

parts.note: a slant is an inclination or slope

explanation.surface: A woman who prefers not to respond to a man's advances.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a man who pays court to a woman, offering inclination 'from him'. 'to ignore overture' removes the S of SLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant is a man attentive and courteous to women, the source of romantic interest towards a female.

clue.text: Support overthrow of alien state, oddly

indicators.note: to overthrow is to turn over, so the letters picked are read backwards
taking letters at odd intervals, every other one, from the phrase

explanation.surface: A political report: the toppling of a strange regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes alternate letters of 'alien state', here LESAE, and 'overthrow of' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that supports a painter's canvas or a board.

clue.text: A nation welcomes former queen and king

indicators.note: a host welcomes a guest in, so the nation's letters take the next piece inside

parts.note: a land is a country or nation
ex means former, as in ex-wife
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A country receives an ex-monarch and her consort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'king' is the definition, not K: Alexander was a king's name. 'welcomes' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Several kings bore the name, most famously Alexander the Great of Macedon and three Scottish monarchs.

clue.text: Father's spoken about one sort of wall decoration

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father; the possessive is a link

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the spoken word goes round the next piece

parts.note: oral means spoken rather than written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Dad has talked about one type of interior décor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; the possessive on 'Father's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A moulding fixed along a wall at waist height, a classic interior decorating feature.

clue.text: Talent shown by mummer performing in Scottish town

parts.note: a mummer is a mime actor, performing in dumb show, so mummer suggests dumb
art is skill or talent
on means performing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: A mime artist shows off ability while performing in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown by' is a link; the pieces run DUMB, ART, ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbarton is a town on the River Clyde in west-central Scotland.

clue.text: Bovine: cow with no tail

indicators.note: a tail is an end, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate or bully them

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style note on a tailless cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' is the verb meaning intimidate, not the animal; 'with no tail' drops the Y of BULLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull is a male bovine animal, an example of the cattle family.

clue.text: Deer mostly can dart up mountain peak

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the assembled letters are read from the bottom, backwards
most of the word, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: an elk is a large deer
taken as written
to nip is to dart or move quickly

explanation.surface: A deer that can mostly scamper up a mountain to its top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ELK to EL; EL, CAN and NIP are then reversed by 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pinnacle is a high pointed peak of rock or mountain.

clue.text: Among children, a boy appears mature

indicators.note: among puts the next pieces inside the word for children

parts.note: seed means offspring or descendants
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Of all the kids, one lad looks grown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'children' means offspring, seed in the biblical sense; 'Among' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoned means experienced, matured, as wood or a veteran is seasoned over time.

clue.text: Note followed by second note

indicators.note: the first piece comes first and the next is placed after it

parts.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale
mo is short for moment, a second

explanation.surface: A musical note, then another one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second note' reads as one phrase, but 'second' gives MO and 'note' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a short written note or memorandum.

clue.text: Keeping mum out of part of hospital is senseless

indicators.note: the hospital department sits within the word for senseless, being placed in it

parts.note: silly means foolish or senseless
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department

explanation.surface: A mother discharged from a hospital ward is confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like a mother but means silent; 'is' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep mum is to say nothing, so doing something without a word is keeping mum.

clue.text: Aromatic plant appealing to the taste buds, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so this is a word that sounds like the other

parts.note: savoury means tasty, pleasing to the palate

explanation.surface: A fragrant herb said to be delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: The herb is spelt without a U, the adjective with one; they sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Savory is a herb of the mint family used in cooking, prized for its fragrance.

clue.text: Thus has aversion to everything?

definitions.meaning: read cryptically: likes nothing, O being nothing, a person who dislikes everything

explanation.surface: A question: so, does someone loathe everything?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as LIKES O: someone who likes O, nothing, has an aversion to everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrase used while demonstrating something: do it in this manner, just so.

clue.text: A soldier at military base heading off trouble

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: the heading, the first letter, is taken off

parts.note: a station is a military base or post

explanation.surface: A soldier at a base sets off to deal with some disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like departing, but it removes the S of STATION; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: agitation is disturbance, unrest or trouble.

clue.text: Groups including cults, primarily

indicators.note: the groups take the next letter inside them

parts.note: sets are groups or collections

indicators.note: first of all, so only the first letter of cults is used

explanation.surface: A description of bodies of people, cults chiefly among them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: religious groups, cults among them. 'primarily' picks C, which 'including' puts in SETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sects are religious factions or denominations, a category that cults belong to.

clue.text: It takes twenty-four hours that's right —— to make spicy food

parts.note: Sat, Saturday, is one day of twenty-four hours
ay (aye) means yes, that's right

explanation.surface: A recipe that needs a whole day to prepare a hot dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twenty-four hours' stands for one particular day, Saturday, shortened to SAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay is a South-East Asian dish of spiced meat on skewers with peanut sauce.

clue.text: First sign of trouble over faulty power cable

indicators.note: the first sign is the initial letter

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: faulty means not working right, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An early warning of a defective electrical cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' is the anagram signal, giving WROPE; 'power cable' wants to be one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A tow rope is a strong line or cable used for pulling a vehicle.

clue.text: Maybe page in legal document not right?

indicators.note: the word for right is left out

parts.note: a contract is a binding legal document

explanation.surface: Perhaps a page in a legal agreement is incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'page' looks like a sheet of paper but is the verb: to page someone is to contact them.
explanation.definitionFit: Paging someone, by pager or tannoy, is one example of getting in touch, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Finally detain suspect making a stink

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word

parts.note: iffy means dubious or suspect

explanation.surface: A suspect at last held, and kicking up a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a stink' looks like making a fuss but means literally smelly. NIFFY is informal British for smelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Niff is British slang for a bad smell, so niffy means smelly, giving off a pong.

clue.text: Nothing to do when visiting islands, of course

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

indicators.note: a visitor goes in, so this word is placed inside the islands

parts.note: keys are low coral islands, as in the Florida Keys; two of them here
taken as written

explanation.surface: Idle holidaymakers with nothing to do on islands.
explanation.walkthrough: DO goes inside a pair of KEYs (islands), after O.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal expression of agreement, like 'certainly' or 'all right'.
